label: Total Crossings (Jul 30 - Aug 4)
source: House of Commons Library / CNN / Ceuta city government
contestNote: Spanish Interior Ministry initially said 49,000-50,000 in 24 hours; Mayor Vivas said 60,000; cumulative full-crisis estimates range up to 80,000.

label: Confirmed Deaths
source: PM Sánchez, Congress address (Sep 3) / House of Commons Library
contestNote: Rose from an initial 72 (Aug 2) to 86 (Sky News) to 111 (100 in Ceuta, 11 in Fnideq) by Aug 4; some later-recovered bodies not definitively linked to the crisis. PM Sánchez cited an official cumulative toll of 141 in his Sep 3 Congress address without detailing the new count's methodology — coincidentally matching NGO Caminando Fronteras' Aug 5 tally (78 in Spanish waters, 63 in Moroccan waters), though officials have not confirmed the figures share the same underlying data. A one-month retrospective by The Olive Press (Aug 30) had already cited 'more than 150' deaths, the highest figure reported to date.

label: Returned to Morocco
source: Spanish government (Aug 3)

label: Migrants Still in Ceuta
source: Spanish government officials via port-transfer operation coverage (Sep 18)
contestNote: Officials revised the working estimate sharply upward on Sep 18, roughly doubling the previous 5,000 figure, after the Poniente port camp transfer exposed a larger-than-assumed street population; ~6,000 are now in official facilities and 3,000-4,000 remain on streets or beaches. Ceuta president Vivas had already put his own estimate around 13,000 as of Sep 13, while security-force sources cited Sep 15 put it closer to 16,000. Ceuta's Assembly unanimously declared the city in an 'extreme situation, on the verge of collapse' on Aug 28.

label: Beach Camp Migrants Relocated to Shelters
source: Euronews (Aug 21)
contestNote: Transferred to two new temporary reception centres, Loma Margarita and El Embolsamiento (1,800 combined initial capacity), as police cleared the El Trampolín beach camp. About 500 people returned to the beach hours later, forcing a second eviction attempt Aug 21; Ceuta city government warned it would suspend beach-cleaning operations if migrants kept returning. Migration Minister Elma Saiz says capacity could expand to ~4,000 places via four additional sites.

label: Unaccompanied Minors Identified
source: Minister Ángel Víctor Torres, post-Council of Ministers presser (Sep 22)
contestNote: Torres reported 2,321 minors formally registered ('filiados') as of Sep 22 — up from ~1,478 registered Sept 1 — with roughly 2,000 already in shelter services and estimates of those still unaccounted for on the streets ranging from 500-700 (Sep 22 presser) to 'a thousand' (Sep 23 remarks blaming the PP). A new 500-700 place camp at Cuesta Caballería was announced Sep 22 to expand capacity beyond the earlier 29-place shelter baseline.

label: CETI Reception Centre Occupancy
source: InfoMigrants
contestNote: Unaccompanied-minors facility separately reported at 2,400% of ordinary capacity per Mayor Vivas.

label: EU States Imposing Border Checks on Spain
source: 2026 Ceuta migrant crisis — Wikipedia
contestNote: Italy, France, Finland, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Czechia had each reimposed or announced border controls linked to the crisis.

label: Italy-Spain Schengen Suspension Runs Until
source: Moncloa.com / Infobae (Sep 15-16)
contestNote: Extended a fourth time: Italy's Interior Ministry under Matteo Piantedosi pushed its checks on Spanish arrivals to roughly end of September, citing 'high internal security risks' and possible terrorist infiltration; Spain replied within hours with a reciprocal 15-day extension of checks on Italian arrivals, moving its own deadline from Sep 22 to Oct 8. Foreign Minister Albares called Rome's move 'absurd, useless and a disgrace,' saying there is 'no risk or threat to the integrity of the Schengen area arising from Ceuta and Melilla.'

label: Hate Speech Posts Logged (Jul 30-31 crossing window)
source: OBERAXE via Euronews (Aug 25)
contestNote: Logged over the two days of the mass crossing alone; part of a broader jump to 57,406 hate-content items in July, up from 40,800 in June. 48% of posts link migration to crime and 40% dehumanise targeted groups.

label: New Urgent Reception Places Approved
source: PM Sánchez, 'El Intermedio' interview via El Español (Sep 14)
contestNote: Capacity rose from 1,800 (Sept 1) to roughly 4,300-4,500 by Sept 13-14 with the Los Rosales tent facility (864 places), then Sánchez raised the target sharply on Sep 14, saying the government aims for close to 10,000 activated places with ~6,000 expected by week's end — up from the 500 places available when the crisis began. Analysts note the higher target sits awkwardly with the government's parallel claim that most arrivals have already been returned to Morocco.

label: Voluntary Returns to Morocco (Since Aug 10 Program)
source: Minister Ángel Víctor Torres, post-Council of Ministers presser (Sep 22)
contestNote: Distinct from the earlier '~70,000 returned' KPI, which captured the mass same-day/same-week turnbacks immediately after the Jul 30-31 crossing. This figure tracks a formal government return program for migrants who remained in Ceuta, running since Aug 10: 6,791 voluntary returns as of Sep 22, plus 318 formal expulsions — up from 5,482 returns as of Sep 15.

label: Ceuta Business Losses (as of Aug 11)
source: Tourism & Society TT / FTNnews
contestNote: Includes an estimated €10.2M from the cancelled patron-saint festivities alone, plus ~90% August tourism booking cancellations.

label: New Emergency Economic Package for Ceuta
source: Spanish Council of Ministers via Euronews (Aug 30)
contestNote: Sept 1 decree-law: €118M humanitarian/minors' care, €90M security, €80M economic activity support, €21M essential services, plus €50M in loan guarantees, for the remainder of 2026. Supersedes the €165M figure announced Aug 30 (€80M near-term Ceuta economy injection + €70M for 2027), which government officials describe as folded into this broader package rather than additive to it.

label: EU Emergency Migration Funds Requested by Spain
source: Spanish government via Euronews / Libertad Digital (Aug 24)
contestNote: Requested from the EU's FAMI (Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund) and IGFV (Borders and Visa Instrument) to help cover Ceuta's reception, triage and border-management costs. Brussels confirmed Sep 4 it will send a technical mission to Ceuta to convert the request into specific measures, following a Marlaska-Brunner call citing 'important progress.'

label: New Port Reception Capacity (Tents)
source: The Objective / COPE / El Español (Sep 17-18)
contestNote: 16,000 m² of Ceuta port's Poniente dock authorised for temporary migrant tents after the Ceuta Port Authority's own board voted against the installation; Madrid invoked Article 73.3 of the State Ports and Merchant Marine Act to proceed regardless. Spain's National Court rejected a police union's bid to block the camp's opening on Sep 17. It opened Sep 18 with roughly 1,700 places but over 3,000 people were moved from the Trampolín/Benítez beach camps, producing chaotic overcrowded scenes.

label: Ceuta Land Arrivals 2026 (Jan-Aug, excl. Jul crossing)
source: Spanish Interior Ministry via Moncloa.com (Sep 3)
contestNote: Up 102.3% versus the same period in 2025, explicitly excluding the ~72,000 people from the July 30-31 mass crossing, which the ministry has deferred recording pending completion of triage.

label: Approval of Sánchez's Ceuta Crisis Handling
source: 40dB poll for El País / Cadena SER (Sep 7)
contestNote: Two-thirds of the 2,000 respondents said the government's response was too slow; combined PP+Vox voting intention reached 50.2% in the same poll, the first time the potential right-wing bloc has broken 50% this legislature.

label: New Mass-Crossing Calls Circulating For
value: Sep 23, 2026 — passed calmly (4 arrests, Fnideq clash)
source: Infobae / El Español (Sep 23)
contestNote: Social media calls for renewed mass entries to Ceuta and Melilla circulated for both Sep 20 and Sep 23 (Morocco's election day), including a 200-member WhatsApp group titled 'El gran asalto del 23 de septiembre'; neither date produced a mass crossing. On Sep 23 a group of migrants clashed with Moroccan security forces near Fnideq, resulting in four arrests, but the border otherwise held calm under a reinforced Morocco-Spain security posture and the Rabat embassy's Sep 21 disinformation campaign.

label: Who the Public Blames for the Crossing
source: 40dB poll (Sep 7) vs. Spain's state-run CIS poll under José Félix Tezanos (Sep 14)
contestNote: The independent 40dB poll for El País/Cadena SER (Sep 7) found roughly nine in ten Spaniards blaming Morocco. Spain's own CIS institute, led by a Sánchez appointee, instead found 49.1% blaming the United States and 15.2% Israel, against just 38.1% for Morocco and 1.4% for King Mohammed VI — a divergence critics attribute to CIS's framing under Tezanos rather than a genuine shift in public opinion. Both polls agree on border policy: 82%+ back strengthening the Ceuta/Melilla borders.
